family_judgments.evidence: Cloze and dialogue permit simple-past passive “wasn't tested,” whereas MCQ and cue-driven transformation force past-perfect passive.
The open formats can measure only passive negation in practice, while the transformation explicitly supplies BEEN and imposes the full perfect-passive construction.
All formats concern the alarm not being tested before the drill.

criteria.evidence: The keyed past-perfect passive is targeted, but “wasn't tested” is a linguistically and contextually reasonable completion that avoids perfect HAVE and past finite selection; solver replicate 1 supplied it.
The response does target passive, perfect, past, and negation; no additional major construction is required.
A learner can accurately complete the sentence with simple-past passive “wasn't tested,” avoiding the declared perfect construction.
“The alarm wasn't tested before the drill began” is grammatical and fits the stated record of no earlier test; past perfect is not forced.
The reasonable unkeyed response “wasn't tested” is omitted from the accepted set, so its rejection is blocking.
Safety-alarm context and test are comprehensible for B2 and are not the source of the defect.
Despite the intended target, “wasn't tested” remains a reasonable simple-past passive completion and avoids perfect HAVE.
Dialogue content supports the intended passive-perfect-negative construction without extra major grammar.
The response can be correct in context without performing the declared perfect operation.
The dialogue establishes prior non-testing but does not make past perfect obligatory over simple past passive.
“Wasn't tested” is linguistically/contextually reasonable yet unaccepted; contraction coverage for had not does not cure this alternative.
The preceding paraphrase “No one had checked whether it worked” adds discourse interpretation, though it is manageable.
Option B realizes all four declared operations, and the distractors contrast passive BE, perfect HAVE, and negation.
The choice stays within the stated passive-perfect-negative construction.
The malformed alternatives allow substantial elimination, although no offered option provides a valid target-avoiding answer.
Among the presented options, B alone correctly describes the no-test-before-drill situation.
B is the sole defensible option in this closed response set.
The causal context is explicit and vocabulary is ordinary.
Changing “No one had tested the alarm” into the required subject-initial negative passive actively calls for HAD, NOT, BEEN, and TESTED.
The task additionally requires active-to-passive transformation and combining two source propositions.
The required start and BEEN cue rule out a simple-past passive shortcut.
The cue and explicit unchanged-meaning instruction constrain the target sufficiently.
Both full and contracted negative target forms are accepted; no further reasonable unkeyed response was proposed.
Voice conversion and sentence combination create appreciable burden beyond the component KCs.

summary: Reject: the open completions do not determine past perfect. “Wasn't tested” is a reasonable, unaccepted target-avoiding response and makes format equivalence fail.
